title: Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings: Cultural Developments (c. 600 BCE - 600 CE)

topics.title: A glimpse of Sanchi and the sources

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the rulers of Bhopal and later decisions helped preserve the stupa complex at Sanchi.
Identify the textual and material sources historians use to reconstruct religious ideas of c. 600 BCE - 600 CE.
Describe the early Vedic sacrificial tradition and how sacrifices changed over time.
Explain the new questions about life, rebirth and ultimate reality raised in the Upanishads.
Distinguish the Ajivika and Lokayata positions and explain how historians know about them.

topics.title: The message of Mahavira and the spread of Jainism

concepts.learning_objective: State the central teachings of Jainism, including ahimsa, karma and the five vows.
Describe how Jaina literature and sculpture spread and were preserved.

topics.title: The Buddha, his teachings and Buddhist texts

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how historians reconstruct the Buddha's life from hagiographies and assess their value.
Explain the Buddhist ideas of anicca, anatta, dukkha, the middle path and nibbana.
Identify the three pitakas and how Buddhist texts were compiled, transmitted and preserved.

topics.title: Followers of the Buddha and the sangha

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the organisation, membership and functioning of the Buddhist sangha.
Explain the entry of women into the sangha and interpret verses of the Therigatha.
Analyse why Buddhism appealed to many people in a time of social change.

topics.title: Stupas: why and how they were built

concepts.learning_objective: Identify chaityas and the places associated with the Buddha's life that came to be regarded as sacred.
Explain why stupas were built and why they were venerated.
Describe the structure of a stupa and the patrons who financed its building.

topics.title: Discovering stupas and reading their sculpture

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the fate of the stupas at Amaravati and Sanchi after their discovery.
Interpret symbols used in early Buddhist sculpture by relating them to textual traditions.
Analyse how popular and pre-Buddhist traditions shaped the sculpture at Sanchi.

topics.title: New religious traditions and the limits of what we can see

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the changes in Buddhist ideas and practices that led to Mahayana Buddhism.
Describe the growth of Vaishnavism, Shaivism, the Puranas and early temple architecture.
Evaluate the problems historians face in interpreting unfamiliar images and images that texts do not explain.
